items.title: ASIC flags 35 suspected audit misconduct matters at the Big Four
items.summary: Australia's corporate regulator reviewed thousands of internal complaints at KPMG, Deloitte, EY and PwC and found 35 that raise questions about statutory audit conduct or misuse of client information.
detail: ASIC published the findings of its Big Four surveillance on 25 November. It covered 3,215 internal complaints lodged at the four firms between July 2023 and June 2026, of which 558 related to audit, and 35 raised concerns ranging from misuse of client information to falsified audit work.

Some matters are being considered for enforcement action, and others relate to existing investigations into KPMG, including misstatements in its transparency reporting. KPMG said it is looking at how to improve complaints handling and whistleblower protection, PwC said it keeps improving its processes, and Deloitte and EY welcomed the review.

ASIC Commissioner Kate O'Rourke said the findings strengthen the case for licensing audit firms and for stronger enforcement and disciplinary powers. The review began in July after KPMG Australia's CEO resigned in May over the handling of a whistleblower complaint about client data.
items.why: It is live evidence for the audit regulation debate in Australia, including whether firms, and not only individual auditors, should be licensed.

items.title: Comment period on IASB risk mitigation accounting closes on 30 November
items.summary: Feedback on the IASB's proposed amendments to IFRS 9 and IFRS 7 for risk mitigation accounting is due this Monday, after the Board extended the deadline to match its fieldwork timetable.
detail: The IASB's exposure draft proposes a risk mitigation accounting (RMA) model to replace macro hedge accounting approaches for banks that manage interest rate risk on a net portfolio basis.

The Board extended the comment deadline to 30 November 2026 so it lines up with the deadline for fieldwork results from participating entities. The IASB also expects to publish its feedback statement on the post-implementation review of IFRS 16 Leases in November.
items.why: RMA is the biggest change to IFRS 9 hedge accounting in years and a likely topic in advanced financial accounting units.

items.title: TNFD pushes the ISSB for a mandatory nature standard
items.summary: The TNFD has asked the ISSB to issue a standalone, mandatory standard on nature-related risks, while the ISSB is consulting on voluntary nature guidance as a Practice Statement.
detail: The ISSB's consultation on nature guidance, which would supplement IFRS S1 and S2, closes on 19 February 2027. On 19 November the TNFD called for a standalone standard with a timeline for mandatory application.

The ISSB met in Frankfurt on 18 and 19 November and posted its meeting notes on 23 November. Elsewhere, Thailand's SEC has adopted ISSB-aligned rules starting with SET50 companies for the 2027 financial year.
items.why: Whether nature disclosure becomes mandatory will shape the next stage of AASB S2-style reporting in Australia and Asia.

items.title: Bank of Korea hikes to 3.25%, its third rise this year
items.summary: The Bank of Korea raised its base rate by 25 basis points to 3.25% on 26 November in a 5-2 vote, citing chip-led export growth and inflation above target.
detail: It is the third hike of 2026, after increases in July and August took the rate up from 2.5% to 3% and a pause in October. Board members Hwang Kunil and Lee Soohyung voted to hold.

The bank lifted its 2026 growth forecast to 3.9% from 3.3% and its 2027 inflation forecast to 2.4% from 2.3%. The board's median rate projection for the next six months sits at 3.5%, which points to one more hike.
The move comes ahead of an expected US Federal Reserve hike in December, adding to a wave of tightening across the region that includes Bank Indonesia and the RBA in November.
items.why: It shows how widely Asian central banks are now tightening, which matters for regional currencies including the rupiah.

items.title: Wall Street claws back a 3% slide before Thanksgiving
items.summary: US stocks ended mixed on 25 November after a sharp morning sell-off in AI names, with the S&P 500 down just 0.25% at the close after falling more than 3% intraday.
detail: The Dow rose 0.33% to 50,182.95 after being down more than 1,100 points at its low. The S&P 500 closed at 7,182.78 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.62% to 23,585.80 after dropping as much as about 4.6% during the session.

Selling in AI-related shares, hotter October PCE inflation and new US tariff proposals drove the swings. US markets were shut on 26 November for Thanksgiving and reopen for a half-day session on Friday.
items.why: The intraday whipsaw shows how stretched AI valuations and inflation worries are feeding market volatility into year-end.

items.title: ASX 200 rebounds 0.8% on miners and energy
items.summary: Australian shares rose 71.4 points to 8,763.8 on 26 November as miners and energy stocks recovered after Wall Street pared its losses.
detail: The gain reversed Wednesday's 0.39% fall, which followed the jump in Australian monthly inflation to 4.9%. Materials led the market, with 103 stocks in the ASX 200 higher, 91 lower and six unchanged.
US Treasury yields also eased, with the 10-year falling to about 4.85% on 25 November as investors moved into bonds during the tech sell-off.
items.why: Local equity and bond moves frame the backdrop for the RBA's 7–8 December meeting after its November hike.

items.title: Kenya's minimum top-up tax notification deadline is 30 November
items.summary: Multinational groups in scope of Kenya's new 15% minimum top-up tax must notify the Kenya Revenue Authority of their status by 30 November 2026.
detail: KRA moved the deadline from 17 November to 30 November in a public notice on 9 November. The notification must give the group name, the ultimate parent's jurisdiction and every Kenyan constituent entity with its KRA PIN. Filing a top-up tax return and paying any tax due are separate later steps.

The tax sits in Section 12G of the Income Tax Act, introduced by the Tax Laws (Amendment) Act 2024, and the Income Tax (Minimum Top-Up Tax) Regulations 2026 were published as Legal Notice No. 189 on 18 September 2026.
items.why: It is a concrete example of a developing country building a domestic minimum tax on the Pillar Two template.

items.title: Ireland rejects Costa's EU-wide digital services levy
items.summary: Taoiseach Micheál Martin said Ireland will not back European Council President António Costa's proposal for a 3% EU levy on certain digital revenues of large firms.
detail: Costa has revived the stalled idea of an EU digital levy as a way to fund the next EU budget. The proposal would apply a 3% charge to certain digital revenues of large companies.
Martin said that global taxation has to be done globally, signalling Ireland prefers solutions agreed at the OECD level. The Irish Times reported the exchange on 21 November.
items.why: It shows the EU budget debate reopening digital tax questions that Pillar One was meant to settle.

items.title: Inclusive Framework reports progress on Pillar Two reviews
items.summary: The OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework's statement after its October plenary welcomed the start of full legislative reviews of Pillar Two rules and work on a GloBE coordination mechanism.
detail: The Inclusive Framework met in Paris from 28 to 30 October 2026. Its statement covered the global minimum tax, the tax challenges of digitalisation and global mobility.
EY reports that a safe harbour for de minimis and routine profits is being developed to sit alongside the simplified effective tax rate safe harbour from the January 2026 side-by-side package.
items.why: Legislative reviews will test whether national Pillar Two rules match the model rules, a core issue for qualified status.

items.title: Rupiah sets another record low close at Rp18,364
items.summary: The rupiah closed 0.17% weaker at Rp18,364 per US dollar on 26 November, its weakest close on record, after touching Rp18,403 intraday.
detail: The previous close was Rp18,332 on 25 November. Bank Indonesia's JISDOR reference rate weakened 87 points, or 0.48%, to Rp18,390.

Analysts linked the move to the threat of new US tariffs and thinner global liquidity around the US Thanksgiving holiday. Analyst Ibrahim Assuaibi expects the rupiah to trade between Rp18,360 and Rp18,420 in the next session.
items.why: A weaker rupiah raises the rupiah cost of dollar debt and affects foreign currency translation under PSAK 10.

items.title: IHSG rises 0.86% to 5,242 on year-end window dressing hopes
items.summary: The Jakarta Composite Index gained 44.56 points to 5,242.17 on 26 November, led by energy stocks, with nearly all sectors higher.
detail: The index opened at 5,214.62 and touched 5,297.46 during the day. Trading value reached Rp7.78 trillion. BRPT, AADI and ADRO were among the top LQ45 gainers.

Antara attributed the rise to optimism about year-end window dressing. Investors are watching a proposed US tariff on Indonesia of up to 18%, the Fed's December decision and next week's trade and inflation data.
items.why: The rebound comes despite the record-low rupiah, a split worth tracking for foreign investor flows.

items.title: DJP says higher PPh 25 instalments are not 'ijon pajak'
items.summary: The Directorate General of Taxes denied that raising monthly PPh Article 25 instalments in November and December is a way of collecting next year's tax early.
detail: DJP spokesperson Inge Diana Rismawanti said the adjustment (dinamisasi) reflects growth in a taxpayer's business and actual conditions, and is applied selectively under the rules so the annual tax payment due in April 2027 will be lighter.

Under PER-11/PJ/2025, DJP can raise instalments when the tax expected to be owed exceeds 125% of the base, down from 150% under the old rule. Taxpayers can ask for a reduction if expected tax is below 75% of the base. Apindo has asked DJP to apply the policy selectively.
items.why: It shows how DJP uses instalment rules to protect revenue late in the year, a recurring source of friction with taxpayers.

items.title: DJP backs final income tax for commodity futures and derivatives
items.summary: DJP has agreed in principle to a final income tax (PPh final) scheme for commodity futures and financial derivative trading, and the proposal now goes to the Ministry of Finance.
detail: The Ministry of Finance will discuss the rate and the withholding mechanism. Separately, tax revenue reached Rp1,796.8 trillion by 31 October 2026, or 76.2% of the Rp2,357.7 trillion APBN target, and Finance Minister Suahasil Nazara said looser refund rules for MSMEs and labour-intensive firms will continue into 2027.
items.why: A final tax regime for derivatives would change how gains are taxed and reported for Indonesian traders and brokers.
